item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I like that at least one upvote was specifically given to spite Bright hating on the article. haha

I'm upvoting just because I like it, though. =P

With how hot she burns if not fed or whatever, would flame resistant clothes really make a difference? I think she should just have cheap clothes and that part be taken out, unless her "regular" temperature is high enough that "normal" clothes would combust all the time, and I don't think that was ever really stated in the description or containment procedures.

Only other issue I see is the use of the word "feeding". It says in one paragraph that the scip has no need or desire to eat or drink, then talks about a "hunger" and "feeding" a bunch. I was able to figure it out, but it could probably use a little tweaking to make it more clear that she's being given a few kg of meat to incinerate. It seems like it's stated in a throwaway sentence, then "feeding" is used all over, and it sounds like she needs to EAT 2.5kg every twelve hours, which isn't what I think is meant, otherwise she'd have a "need/desire to eat, but not drink"… right? Or am I reading this entirely incorrectly?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Very, very meh to me. It seems like a lot of focus is put on how she consumes things. When I think a human SCP with kind of freaky powers, I don't think of how they eat. I think of how it affects them. From the interview, it seems like she doesn't want to hurt people and she views herself as demonic, but the rest of the article is really about how she eats things. I don't want to think 'Wow, I want to be this person.' I want to think 'I never want to be this person, let alone be near them.'

I've downvoted the article for now, but I think that you MIGHT be able to save this with a good old fashioned rewrite. Human SCPs are hard to write, honestly, and if this is your first attempt I'd say try again but with something that isn't human. Take a waffleiron and make it weird or something.

This SCP is not intended as a character. If it's coming across as one, I have made an error. Any suggestions for improvement will be appreciated. The purpose was not the creation of a character, but a being that is inherently human but involuntarily monstrous, and the implications of that existence's effects on the subject.

Suggestions can always include removal of large parts of the article. If I had to pick one I personally feel iffy about, it would be the email at the end.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
*soapbox*

If you're thinking of a humanoid SCP as a character, I can safely say it's not going to go well, no matter what you do—because you're fundamentally thinking of it the wrong way. Evidence: Whiny telepath ("Saint"), is dying, but 231 (110-Montauk) isn't. Looking at my attempts: baleeted-795 and baleeted-770 were erased, because they were characters with SCP-like effects. However, the asian girl in 466 is just a host, and that article is at a comfortable +5. Some of the older character-SCPs are getting away with it, but that's because herp derp cant criticize teh classix lol. Yet, 132 isn't looking so good…

TL;DR: SCP characters get deleted.
